_metadata.rubric: x04 rubric (natural-click standard + five content questions), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: Apart from the instructions file, I read only x04b-ra-input.json; I opened no other file, ran no repository search, and used no web or paid API.

hints.reason: BAT via Batman, KNIGHT via The Dark Knight, both protectors of Gotham; a clean, instant Batman click.

pairs.pair_note: GOTHAM and the served DARK are both good; GOTHAM is the more fun of the two.

hints.reason: BAT via Batman and PENGUIN via the Gotham villain; two animals recast as hero and villain is a real 'oh, nice' moment.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best Gotham pairs: both targets look like animals until the hint lands.

hints.reason: BAT via Batman; SCARECROW via the Batman villain (well known from Batman Begins), a second-tier rogue so it takes a beat, but the click is real.

pairs.pair_note: SCARECROW also pulls toward Oz, which is fair misdirection; slightly weaker than PENGUIN.

hints.reason: BOWL via the clay potter's craft, HOGWARTS via Harry Potter; a fair double meaning that clicks nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Good double-meaning use of POTTER; the bowl side needs a half-second shift away from the wizard.

hints.reason: BOWL via a clay potter, WAND via Harry Potter's wand; satisfying two-sense click.

pairs.pair_note: Same double meaning as BOWL+HOGWARTS; equally good.

hints.reason: BROOM via Harry's Quidditch broomstick, HOGWARTS via his school; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: The served QUIDDITCH is a bit more specific and satisfying, but POTTER is also a genuinely good hint; both can stand.

hints.reason: CAR via Cars and MONSTER via Monsters, Inc.; both are Pixar titles, an easy clean click.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, easy Pixar pair.

hints.reason: CAR via traffic jam, PRINTER via paper jam; both phrases are instantly familiar and share the relatable 'stuck' frustration.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase-join that earns its place: both jams are everyday annoyances.

hints.reason: CAR via Cars; ROBOT via WALL-E, which needs one recall step since 'robot' is not in the title, but WALL-E is iconic.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; the robot side is a step less direct than the title-word sides.

hints.reason: CAVE via the Batcave and KNIGHT via The Dark Knight both route through Batman rather than the city itself, so GOTHAM adds a step that BATMAN (Batcave, the Dark Knight) would not; also the Batcave sits beneath Wayne Manor, not under the city.
hints.fix: The Batcave is hidden beneath Wayne Manor, just outside Gotham City.

pairs.pair_note: Both targets are Batman's own things, not the city's; BATMAN is the obvious stronger hint here.

hints.reason: DETECTIVE via Sherlock Holmes himself, LONDON via his Baker Street home; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, solid.

hints.reason: DETECTIVE via Holmes's job, PIPE via his iconic pipe; instant classic image.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and iconic.

hints.reason: DETECTIVE is Sherlock's job, but SUSPECT is reached only through 'detectives deal with suspects', not anything Sherlock-specific, so the hint is lopsided; ALIBI (a detective checks it, a suspect gives it) hits both evenly.

pairs.pair_note: The pair itself is directly related; a hint should sit between them (ALIBI, CLUE) rather than on top of DETECTIVE.

hints.reason: FAIRYTALE via ogres as fairy-tale monsters; DONKEY via Shrek's sidekick, one quick step from OGRE to Shrek.

pairs.pair_note: SHREK would also work (Donkey; a fairy-tale parody), but OGRE is not clearly weaker.

hints.reason: GREEN via Shrek the green ogre, DONKEY via Shrek's best friend; OGRE leads straight to Shrek, so both land.

pairs.pair_note: Works through the Shrek image; fine.

hints.reason: SHREK is the famous ogre and DONKEY is his best friend; easy, with Donkey one short step away.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; OGRE is Shrek's species, not a synonym of the target.

hints.reason: DRAFT via draft pick (choose) and POCKET via pickpocket (steal); both instantly familiar, with a pleasant shift in sense.

pairs.pair_note: Good phrase-join; the two senses of 'pick' add a little twist.

hints.reason: FAIRYTALE via ogres as fairy-tale monsters, GREEN via Shrek's green skin; the green side leans on Shrek but that image is universal.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; GREEN is the softer side since many things are green.

hints.reason: FAIRYTALE via ogres in fairy tales, LAYER via Shrek's famous 'ogres have layers' line; the quote makes it a fun click.

pairs.pair_note: The layers quote carries this nicely.

hints.reason: FISH via Finding Nemo, LAMP via the hopping-lamp logo before every Pixar film; the lamp is a satisfying 'oh, right' moment.

pairs.pair_note: The logo lamp is the fun half of any PIXAR pair.

hints.reason: FISH via Finding Nemo, MONSTER via Monsters, Inc.; easy Pixar click.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, solid.

hints.reason: GLASSES via Harry's round specs and LIGHTNING via his scar; together they draw his face, an instant and satisfying picture.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent visual pair; the two targets are the two things everyone draws on Harry.

hints.reason: GREEN via Shrek's green skin and LAYER via his 'ogres have layers' line; both are signature Shrek, a fun click.

pairs.pair_note: Strong Shrek pair without naming Shrek.

hints.reason: GUITAR via a guitar pick and ICE via an ice pick; two different tools named PICK, both instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and easy.

hints.reason: GUITAR via a guitar pick, LOCK via picking a lock; noun versus verb sense, both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and easy.

hints.reason: GUITAR via a guitar pick, POCKET via picking pockets; two clear senses of PICK.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and easy.

hints.reason: HAT via the deerstalker and PIPE via his pipe; together they are the Sherlock silhouette, an instant visual click.

pairs.pair_note: Best of the Sherlock pairs: the two props are the costume.

hints.reason: ICE via an ice pick, LOCK via picking a lock (a lock pick); both familiar and easy.

pairs.pair_note: Fine phrase-join; both are tools called picks.

hints.reason: ICE via an ice pick, POCKET via pickpocket; both compounds instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Fine, easy phrase-join.

hints.reason: KNIGHT via The Dark Knight's city; NEW YORK via Gotham as the city's real nickname (and Batman's model city), which many know and the rest enjoy learning.

pairs.pair_note: The NYC nickname is a nice reveal; not everyone knows it, but it is widely referenced.

hints.reason: KNIGHT via The Dark Knight, PENGUIN via the Gotham villain; hero and villain of the same city, easy once Batman comes to mind.

pairs.pair_note: BATMAN would work equally well; GOTHAM is fine.

hints.reason: LAMP via the Pixar logo lamp, RAT via Ratatouille's cooking rat; a fun pairing of two unlikely words.

pairs.pair_note: Strong: neither word looks Pixar-ish until the hint lands.

hints.reason: SHREK is the famous ogre and LAYER comes from his 'ogres have layers' line; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: The served ONION is the more delightful hint, but OGRE is also genuinely good (it is literally the quote); both can stand.

hints.reason: LONDON via his Baker Street home, PIPE via his iconic pipe; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: LONDON is Holmes's city, but STREET is reached only through the 'Baker Street' address, and a word as generic as STREET is unlikely to be picked from SHERLOCK; the explanation also states the Baker Street fact twice.
hints.fix: Sherlock Holmes is London's most famous detective, and he lives at 221B Baker Street.

pairs.pair_note: Both sides lean on the same Baker Street fact, so the two lines barely differ; no obviously better one-word hint comes to mind.

hints.reason: LONDON via Baker Street; VIOLIN via Holmes's violin playing, a real deeper cut from the books and the Cumberbatch and Downey versions that takes a moment of thought; unsure how many casual players know it.

pairs.pair_note: A pleasant deeper-cut fact; worth a second opinion on how familiar the violin is.

hints.reason: NEW YORK via Gotham as the city's nickname, PENGUIN via the Gotham villain; a fun two-sense click for those who know the nickname.

pairs.pair_note: Nice twist pair; the NYC side depends on knowing the nickname.

hints.reason: OWL via Hedwig and owl post, WHEEL via the potter's wheel; two unrelated words joined by two senses of POTTER, a real 'oh, nice'.

pairs.pair_note: Best POTTER pair in the batch: both sides are strong and the senses are fully different.

hints.reason: OWL via Hedwig, WIZARD via the boy wizard himself; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy.

hints.reason: PRINTER via a paper jam, TOAST via jam the spread; a crisp, funny double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning; better than CAR+PRINTER because the senses differ.

hints.reason: RAT via Ratatouille, TOY via Toy Story; easy Pixar click, but Toy Story was Pixar's first feature film, not its first movie (Pixar made earlier shorts).
hints.fix: Toy Story was Pixar's first feature film.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; small accuracy fix on the TOY line.

hints.reason: ROBOT via WALL-E, TOY via Toy Story; easy, with the same 'first feature film' wording fix on the TOY line.
hints.fix: Toy Story was Pixar's first feature film.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; ROBOT needs one WALL-E step.

hints.reason: WIZARD via the boy wizard, SPELL via the spells central to Harry Potter; flat because the two targets are directly related anyway, but clear and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and unexciting; acceptable, not a highlight.
